review: The print gives stanza 1 as two long lines (the refrain quoted twice, then answered) and stanzas 2–5 as four lines; the payload follows the print, so `hebrew-meter.mjs` reports the shape 2/4/4/4 as irregular by construction.

1:1–1:2 הוּא יוֹלִיכֵנִי … בְּיָדוֹ יֹאחֲזֵנִי — Psalm 139:10 (תֹּאחֲזֵנִי יְמִינֶךָ) and Ps 23:3; the Arabic يَقُودُنِي … بِيَدِهِ يُمْسِكُنِي is the leading and the holding, and Hebrew keeps both participles.

2:2–2:3 בְּיָד יָמִין / יַנְחֵנִי — Psalm 16:8 and 73:23 (בִּימִינִי תָּמַכְתָּ); the Arabic بِالْحُبِّ وَالْيَدِ الْيَمِين is 'in love and the right hand', and the Hebrew keeps the hand as the instrument of guidance.
4:2 לֹא אֲבַקֵּשׁ אִישׁ זוּלָתֶךָ — Psalm 73:25; the Arabic لَا أَبْتَغِي شَخْصًا سِوَاك uses شَخْص ('person'), and אִישׁ is the Hebrew equivalent in that sense, as in hymns 94 and 121.

5:3–5:4 לֹא אִירָא חֶשְׁכַּת הַמָּוֶת / אֶעֱלֶה לִנְצָחִים — Psalm 23:4 (צַלְמָוֶת) and the ascent of Rev 11:12; the Arabic لَنْ أَخْشَى ظُلْمَةَ الْمَوْتِ / أَرْقَى لِلْأَبَدِيَّةِ is that pair, and חֶשְׁכָּה is the biblical noun for darkness.
